results.title: 1/5 Respectfully, the facts point the other way.
results.description:
1/5
Respectfully, the facts point the other way. Niger isn't a side issue, it's Algiers' gateway to the whole Sahel. Look at 2026 alone:

🇳🇪 Feb: Tiani in Algiers, ties normalised
🇳🇪 Aug: Su-30s deployed to Niamey
🇳🇪 Oct: military protocol, then the Senate approves troops, a first since 1973
🇳🇪 40 MW power plant gifted, Kafra oil block

Source: Al Jazeera https://t.co/On3gRob3i8

2/5
And Mali? Algiers got back in through Niamey.

🇲🇱 Jul 10: ambassadors back, airspace reopened, a thaw that was mediated by Niger
🇧🇫 $88M mining & energy package for Burkina
🇲🇷 Oct 22: Algeria–Mauritania military security meeting in Zouérat

Niger is the door to Bamako, not a detour.

Source: International Crisis Group https://t.co/l6OjcX1aav

3/5
Now add Ankara 🇹🇷:

• TB2 & Karayel-SU drones in Niger, Turkish instructors on Nigerien bases since April
• Tiani's first trip outside Africa was to Ankara in June
• Turkey trained Malian commandos

Algiers & Ankara set up a strategic council in May, aim for $10B in trade, and share one rival in the region: the UAE.

Source: Turkish Minute https://t.co/3q4NmLZjiY

4/5
That's an alliance of convenience, not a bloc, but it works: Turkey sells & trains, Algeria brings troops, gas and money.

On Russia, I agree it's entrenched. But it's Africa Corps that saved Tiani in August, and Algiers is shoring up Russia's clients, not fighting them. The three are compatible.

Source: Steptoe https://t.co/a4AZBO34GU

5/5
Why it matters for Morocco 🇲🇦:

• The Atlantic Initiative needs the AES capitals to want Dakhla
• Trans-Saharan gas pipeline (via Niger) vs Nigeria–Morocco pipeline
• Whoever secures Niamey sits on both routes

The Sahara file is closing. The Sahel file is wide open. Ignoring Niger means handing it over.

Source: ISS Africa
